title: Punishments
old_text: IPC Section 53 listed five punishments: Death, Imprisonment for life, Imprisonment (rigorous or simple), Forfeiture of property, and Fine.
new_text: The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are: Death, Imprisonment for life, Imprisonment (rigorous or simple), Forfeiture of property, Fine, and Community service.
punishment_new: Introduces 'Community service' as an express sixth category of punishment in Indian criminal jurisprudence.
explanation: BNS Section 4 replaces IPC 53 and adds 'Community service' as a statutory punishment. This provides reformative alternatives for petty offences like defamation and first-time theft under ₹5,000.

title: Commutation of Sentence
old_text: IPC 54 provided for commutation of death sentence; IPC 55 provided for commutation of sentence of imprisonment for life.
new_text: The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute death sentence to any other punishment, or imprisonment for life to imprisonment for a term not less than seven years, or lesser punishments.
punishment_old: Government commutation powers under IPC 54 and 55.
punishment_new: Consolidated commutation powers with statutory minimum floors.
explanation: Section 5 merges IPC Sections 54 and 55 into a unified commutation provision. It allows the appropriate Government to commute capital or life sentences without the offender's consent.

title: Fractions of Terms of Punishment
old_text: In calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life shall be reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.
new_text: In calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life shall be reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.
punishment_old: Calculation standard: Life imprisonment reckoned as 20 years for fractions.
punishment_new: Calculation standard: Life imprisonment reckoned as 20 years for fractions.
explanation: This provision is verbatim renumbered from IPC Section 57 to BNS Section 6. It establishes the legal fiction that life imprisonment equals 20 years solely for mathematical fraction calculations (e.g., attempt).

title: Sentence May be Wholly or Partly Rigorous or Simple
old_text: In every case in which an offender is punishable with imprisonment which may be of either description, it shall be competent to the Court to direct that such imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous, or wholly simple, or that any part shall be rigorous and the rest simple.
new_text: In every case in which an offender is punishable with imprisonment which may be of either description, it shall be competent to the Court to direct that such imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous, or wholly simple, or that any part shall be rigorous and the rest simple.
punishment_old: Discretion of court to award rigorous or simple imprisonment.
punishment_new: Discretion of court to award rigorous or simple imprisonment.
explanation: IPC Section 60 is renumbered as Section 7 of BNS without change. It gives sentencing courts discretion to divide prison terms into rigorous or simple labor segments.

title: Amount of Fine, Default Imprisonment and Recovery
old_text: IPC Sections 63 to 70 governed amount of fine, default imprisonment term limits (1/4th rule), nature of default imprisonment, termination on payment, and 6-year recovery period.
new_text: Consolidates fine rules: fine shall not be excessive; court may order imprisonment in default; default imprisonment cannot exceed one-fourth of maximum term; default imprisonment ceases upon payment; fine leviable within six years or during imprisonment.
punishment_new: Unified fine framework under BNS Section 8.
explanation: BNS Section 8 consolidates eight distinct IPC sections (63 to 70) regarding fines, default imprisonment, and recovery into a unified section. Key safeguards like the one-fourth default imprisonment cap and termination upon payment are preserved.

title: Limit of Punishment of Offence Made Up of Several Offences
old_text: Where anything which is an offence is made up of parts, any of which parts is itself an offence, the offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless expressly provided.
new_text: Where anything which is an offence is made up of parts, any of which parts is itself an offence, the offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless expressly provided.
punishment_old: Prohibition of cumulative punishments for composite acts.
punishment_new: Prohibition of cumulative punishments for composite acts.
explanation: IPC Section 71 is renumbered as Section 9 of BNS. It prevents multiple punishments for composite criminal transactions, such as striking a victim 50 times with a stick.

title: Punishment Where Judgment Doubtful of Which Offence Guilty
old_text: In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences, but it is doubtful of which, the offender shall be punished for that offence for which the lowest punishment is provided.
new_text: In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences, but it is doubtful of which, the offender shall be punished for that offence for which the lowest punishment is provided.
punishment_old: Offender receives the lowest punishment among the alternative offences.
punishment_new: Offender receives the lowest punishment among the alternative offences.
explanation: IPC Section 72 is renumbered as BNS Section 10. When the court is certain an accused committed one of several offences but is doubtful as to which one, sentencing defaults to the lowest punishment.

title: Solitary Confinement
old_text: Court may order solitary confinement for rigorous imprisonment not exceeding three months in the whole (up to 1 month for <= 6 months sentence; up to 2 months for <= 1 year; up to 3 months for > 1 year).
new_text: Court may order solitary confinement for rigorous imprisonment not exceeding three months in the whole according to the statutory sliding scale based on the sentence duration.
punishment_old: Solitary confinement capped at 3 months maximum.
punishment_new: Solitary confinement capped at 3 months maximum.
explanation: IPC Section 73 is renumbered as Section 11 of BNS. It limits solitary confinement to cases of rigorous imprisonment with a maximum ceiling of 3 months.

title: Limit of Solitary Confinement
old_text: Solitary confinement shall not exceed fourteen days at a time, with intervals between periods; when sentence exceeds three months, not to exceed seven days in any one month with like intervals.
new_text: Solitary confinement shall not exceed fourteen days at a time, with intervals between periods; when sentence exceeds three months, not to exceed seven days in any one month with like intervals.
punishment_old: Periodic interval limits to protect physical and mental health.
punishment_new: Periodic interval limits to protect physical and mental health.
explanation: IPC Section 74 is renumbered as Section 12 of BNS. It enforces strict breaks and limits solitary confinement to no more than 14 days at a stretch to safeguard prisoner health.

title: Enhanced Punishment for Certain Offences After Previous Conviction
old_text: Whoever, having been convicted of an offence relating to coin or Government stamp (Chapter XII) or property (Chapter XVII) punishable with 3 years, commits a subsequent offence punishable with 3 years, is liable to life imprisonment or 10 years.
new_text: Whoever, having been convicted of an offence relating to coin, notes or stamps (Chapter X) or property (Chapter XVII) punishable with 3 years, commits a subsequent offence, is liable to imprisonment for life or up to 10 years.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years.
explanation: BNS Section 13 replaces IPC 75, updating chapter cross-references for repeat offenders in property, counterfeiting, and currency crimes. Repeat convictions can elevate sentences to life imprisonment.
